purpose: Current operational router for archive and collection work. This file supersedes earlier priority snapshots for day-to-day research. It does not alter the frozen surviving-object census.
principle: Prioritize the next source that can close a relation, not the next institution that can add a collection name.

targets.target: Charles Elcock — Whipple + St Andrews + Type Slide documentary lineage
targets.status: S+; commercial product, market reception and distributed survival already closed at series/form level
targets.closed: 1885 Type Slide Nos. 1–2 advertisements and retailer network match Whipple drawers explicitly labelled TYPE SLIDE No. 1/2; 1885 display and wanted/exchange evidence show public recognition and secondary demand; St Andrews preserves six independent TYPE SLIDE / OSTRACODA examples; Whipple retains a manuscript sheet (6601.10) apparently listing specimens on slide/s; the later Heron-Allen/Earland Type Slide Collection includes some earliest slides marked Charles Elcock and preserves a key/index architecture.
targets.next: First verify the 1882 Postal Microscopical Society Type Slide review directly in BHL; then request high-resolution Whipple 6601.10, 6601.11, drawers 9–12 and representative Type Slides. Separately transcribe the 2024 Flints Challenger-cabinet labels before treating the cabinet as secure provenance.
targets.payoff: Collection/preparation method → spatial taxonomic matrix → printed/list key → retail product → display/secondary demand → workshop reference archive → distributed reference-collection afterlife.

targets.target: Quekett Microscopical Club + Oxford RMS collections
targets.closed: Cole publication architecture and institutional Library/Cabinet separation are documented; major society slide collections survive.
targets.next: Search existing QMC label transcription for Cole/Martin/Prize Medal/Studies and diagnostic Volume I subjects; query Oxford old slide indexes against a small set of itemised RMS events.
targets.payoff: Published issue/donation event → historical cabinet record → surviving slide.

targets.target: University of Tokyo Medical Library — Anatomy Department nos. 110, 118–123
targets.closed: Course diary, preparation quantity ledger, manufactured histology/embryology catalogue, microscope/instrument index and practical microscopy records are identified as a coherent 1870s–1880s sequence.
targets.next: Acquire page images with covers and original order; extract columns/numbering first; then test preparation categories across production, instrument and teaching records.
targets.payoff: Potential independent paper on institutional production of practical microscopy in Meiji Japan.

targets.target: Cambridge Museum of Zoology / Whipple — Balfour objectives, serial sections and microtome
targets.status: S+ route; publication captions can potentially date instrument acquisition
targets.closed: Balfour embryological sections survive; Whipple preserves a Balfour objective set with Zeiss/Gundlach designations and serial/engraved numbers; the museum explicitly states that acquisition dates for some lenses can be traced through their mentions in plate captions. A pre-1880 Rudolf Jung sliding microtome from Zoology is the type Foster and Balfour described as the microtome they were most accustomed to.
targets.next: Extract every objective/magnification reference from Balfour plate captions before asking for broad archive material. Crosswalk those printed references to objective markings, then to taxon/stage and surviving slide-series candidates. Treat the 1882 engraved F.M.B. dates as potentially commemorative, as the museum warns.
targets.payoff: Objective address → dated plate caption → anatomical preparation/series → surviving section. This is an instrument-use chain rather than instrument biography.

targets.target: Harvard Embryological Collection + Charles Sedgwick Minot papers
targets.status: S/A+; exceptionally rich public crosswalk and strongest seriality-without-publication control
targets.closed: HEC preserves serial sections, original card catalogue, line drawings, previous HEC numbers, current MCZ numbers, technique fields, publication citations and ledger links. Public records demonstrate that old and new addresses can coexist in one object record.
targets.next: Date-filter HEC records to pre-1900 first. Sample a few complete series through old HEC number → card/drawing → section plane/stain/thickness/preparator → publication → current MCZ number. Use later records only to demonstrate catalogue architecture, not as nineteenth-century evidence.
targets.payoff: Controlled distinction: anatomical seriality is not automatically material publication; HEC is also a positive control for relation survival under modern recataloguing.

targets.target: Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn Historical Archives + St Andrews surviving Naples slides
targets.status: S; catalogue/shipment bridge plus surviving external collection
targets.closed: Nine of the twelve June 1880 RMS slides strongly match numbered Naples catalogue offerings. St Andrews independently preserves a named group of Stazione Zoologica Napoli slides and identifies Fritz Meyer as a major preparer of surviving examples.
targets.next: Search 1879–1881 preparation-department accounts, copybooks and A. W. Waters correspondence using matched catalogue numbers and shipment date; simultaneously transcribe St Andrews Naples labels to see whether catalogue numbers or Meyer attributions survive.
targets.payoff: Catalogue → internal order/dispatch → British shipment → independently surviving institutional slides.

targets.target: Museo de La Plata — Tempère & Peragallo / Möller + Historical Archive
targets.closed: Named historical slide series survive in the same museum that preserves institutional correspondence from 1884 onward.
targets.next: Get current series inventory and label/box photographs first; then search acquisition/exchange correspondence by exact names and series numbers.

targets.target: St Andrews Norman + Whipple Wheeler/Watson trade-attribution layer
targets.status: S; catalogue-to-object route now expanded into maker/retailer/collector attribution
targets.closed: St Andrews documents Norman's 1872 list of 2,584 mounts and warns that Norman supplied other mounters/retailers and that secondary labels survive. Whipple's Wheeler 'Planet Mars' slide retains maker mark, Watson retailer label, collector monogram/number and current museum accession, while the exact subject appears in Wheeler's 1876 catalogue.
targets.next: Transcribe St Andrews Norman object labels and physical label layering; exact-title match only those objects against the 1872 catalogue. Use the Wheeler/Watson Mars slide as the model schema for maker → seller → collector → museum transitions.
targets.payoff: Trade history becomes multi-layer attribution rather than a single maker field.

targets.target: University of Coimbra — Costa Simões 1873 catalogue
targets.status: A+; paper system strong, object survival open
targets.closed: One publication joins the histology/physiology course programme, microscopic-preparation collection and experimental-physiology apparatus with 92 engravings.
targets.next: Row-level parse before any archival enquiry; then use category/item names to ask whether original preparations/apparatus survive.
targets.payoff: Published institutional teaching system and a controlled comparison with Tokyo's internal ledgers.

targets.target: Manchester Gibson cabinet / Whipple Pritchard cabinet / Dundee maker series
targets.closed: These surviving cabinets expose maker labels, tray/order information or catalogue-derived labels that can decide which trade catalogues deserve full extraction.
targets.next: Transcribe labels first; then select catalogue rows. Preserve Manchester's published 22-versus-25-tray discrepancy as dated states until the current inventory is checked.
targets.payoff: Buyer cabinet as transaction residue rather than maker catalogue as sole market evidence.

completed_bounded_harvests.result: Five primary letters establish distinct material relations: microscopic preparation for repeat social viewing (1852), scientific consignment of raw material (1880), field preservation failure (1882), professional preparator send-on-approval sale (1885), and gift of a Radiolaria glass collection for microscope viewing (1896).
completed_bounded_harvests.stop_rule: Do not broaden into the whole correspondence. Reopen only for a named preparator, Radiolaria set, transaction, shipment or surviving collection bridge.
